reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a purported one-BNB reward through TokenFlux using a members-only code and pinned link, while tying withdrawal to level-two verification and at least $100 of real-balance activity. The speaker sends 100 USDT and shows a resulting balance, creating a direct reward-to-asset-transfer relationship. Although the process is framed as free educational anti-fraud content, the available video evidence describes a solicitation mechanism involving the transfer of assets.

citations.quote: we're gonna go to TokenFlux.cc and use this secret members only code to claim one whole BNB by doing just these five simple steps
all of the necessary info to complete this process will be in the first pinned comment on YouTube, so I will leave the link to Tokenflux there and the promo code itself
if you're still new on Token Flux and do not have an account, let's complete the first step together by creating our account
use real and working emails that you actually have access to because the second step will be confirming it

our withdrawal is temporarily unavailable because our account does not have level 2 verification and in accordance with the aml kyc policy of tokenflux we need to have a flow of at least a hundred dollars on our real and not bonus balance

opening.argument: The presentation repeatedly places the activity in an educational and risk-aware frame rather than representing crypto participation as guaranteed or consequence-free. The accompanying material expressly says it is educational, warns that crypto trading is risky, urges viewers to do their own research, and says past performance does not guarantee future results. It also teaches viewers how to recognize and avoid fake BNB airdrops. Those warnings are inconsistent with a deceptive certification that the opportunity is automatically safe or profitable.

citations.quote: This video is for educational purposes only. It does not constitute financial advice. Crypto trading is risky.
Past performance is not a guarantee of future results.
How to recognize and avoid fake BNB airdrops

rebuttal.rebuttal: The account setup, pinned information, and verification flow show how to participate, but they do not by themselves establish deception. The speaker expressly distinguishes the transfer from a payment to the platform, describing it as money deposited into the viewer's own account. The prosecution's characterization therefore treats a disclosed verification condition as proof of fraud without showing that the funds were represented as irrecoverable or that the result was guaranteed.

citations.quote: we are not paying token flux 100 usdt in order to claim us one bnb we are depositing this usdt on our own account
this is done to analyze the origin of your funds to pretty much perform an aml screening

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings do not erase the video's concrete call to use a particular platform, code, and account flow. The material supplies the link and promo code in a pinned comment, and withdrawal is unavailable until the account has a hundred dollars of real-balance activity. That operational requirement is more probative of the mechanism than generalized risk language.

citations.quote: all of the necessary info to complete this process will be in the first pinned comment on YouTube, so I will leave the link to Tokenflux there and the promo code itself
our withdrawal is temporarily unavailable because our account does not have level 2 verification
we need to have a flow of at least a hundred dollars on our real and not bonus balance

opening.argument: The central format is a step-by-step operational demonstration: it explains account creation, email confirmation, promo-code activation, withdrawal selection, and wallet interaction. The description calls it a detailed step-by-step tutorial and promises a full walkthrough of the creator's claiming process, including proof of transaction. The speaker presents his own account and experience, then shows a transaction and wallet result. That is consistent with instructional or demonstrative content; it does not establish that viewers are promised the same outcome or that the demonstration is itself a solicitation.

citations.quote: Step-by-Step Breakdown
In this detailed step-by-step tutorial, I’ll show you exactly how I claimed 1 BNB
Full walkthrough of my claiming process
Promo code setup + proof-of-transaction
Here is the transaction

rebuttal.rebuttal: The tutorial framing does not change what the demonstration actually does: it directs viewers to a named external service, supplies a code, and walks through creating an account and attempting withdrawal. Calling this a demonstration describes its format, but not whether the demonstrated process is a legitimate ordinary operation. The content's instructional detail can make the promotion more actionable, rather than remove its promotional character.

citations.quote: we're gonna go to TokenFlux.cc and use this secret members only code to claim one whole BNB
let's complete the first step together by creating our account
I will leave the link to Tokenflux there and the promo code itself

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A tutorial label cannot answer the central evidence that the supposed reward could not be withdrawn until real funds were supplied. The speaker narrates the transfer as the next step after withdrawal failed, then reports verification. Thus the walkthrough is not merely neutral technical education; it models the asset-transfer path needed to unlock the advertised reward.

citations.quote: our withdrawal is temporarily unavailable because our account does not have level 2 verification
send 100 usdt trc 20 over just as specified in the amount given to me by tokenflux
it has already reached my balance and if we go here i see that i am now verified level two

opening.argument: The material can be understood as a promotional reward or service demonstration rather than proof of a scam mechanism. It describes the offer as free to try, with no deposits required, and presents the code as a limited promotional opportunity. When the withdrawal condition appears, the speaker says the USDT remains on the account and is not being paid as a fee. The supplied evidence does not establish a downline scheme, a request for credentials such as a seed phrase, or a guaranteed return to every viewer; it shows a platform workflow and a claimed promotional balance.

citations.quote: 100 % free to try — no deposits required
There are a hundred spots on this promo code.
we are not paying token flux 100 usdt in order to claim us one bnb
we are depositing this usdt on our own account

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of promotional language does not make the offer ordinary commerce. The video's own sequence shows that withdrawal is unavailable until real-balance activity occurs, and the speaker then sends the specified USDT. Whether he calls it a deposit or fee does not remove the condition that viewers must transfer assets to obtain the advertised withdrawal. The transaction requirement is the mechanism at issue.

citations.quote: we need to have a flow of at least a hundred dollars on our real and not bonus balance
send 100 usdt trc 20 over just as specified in the amount given to me by tokenflux

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The claimed balance and later transfer do not make the offer an ordinary giveaway. The reward is introduced through a secret members-only code and the withdrawal attempt fails until the real-balance threshold is met. That sequence shows a low-barrier reward being used to induce an asset transfer, regardless of whether the speaker calls the transfer a deposit or says it remains visible in the account.
